titleEn: Before the Dough, Wash Your Paws!

pages.text: "I want to knead too!" Coco ran in from the alley and hopped up to the dough table. Dark dirt from the alley stones covered their front paws. "Coco, what about your paws?" Mom asked. Coco pretended not to hear.
Coco grabbed the dough and pressed. Push, push! Dark pawprints dotted the white dough. "This is my bread. I'll bake what I made!"
Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks, stopped on his way in. "Oh dear! Dark pawprints in the dough!" Mom lifted it. "There's dirt in here. We can't bake this." Coco pouted.
Mom stood Coco in front of the washbasin. "Before the dough, wash your paws! Just three things. One—get them wet!" Coco dipped both front paws in. The dark dirt began to loosen.

"Two—bubble up with soap!" Coco rubbed their paws together. White bubbles puffed up, soft and lumpy like dough. "Bubble dough!" Beside Coco, Mr. Pig rubbed his big front paws too. "Paws first for me too."
"Three—rinse them clean!" Whoosh! The dark water ran away. After a pat with a towel, Coco's paws were white and dry. Coco held them to their nose and sniffed. "They smell like soap!"
Mom set fresh dough on the table. Coco pressed it. Only clean white marks stayed on the white dough. "Look! Clean prints!" Before the dough, wash your paws!
Coco's bread came out of the oven, the big fiery place where bread bakes. Golden brown, with steam rising. Coco put both front paws on their hips. "Bread I made!" Mr. Pig sniffed the air.
Now Coco didn't forget. "One, get them wet! Two, bubble up with soap! Three, rinse them clean!" The next day, back from the alley, Coco ran to the washbasin before the dough table.
Mom sat beside Coco and gave a snug hug. "We have a paw-washing champion at home!" Clean paws make clean bread. Coco raised their white front paws. "Before the dough, wash your paws!"
